references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew 13:16-17, where Jesus says the same words about many prophets and righteous people wanting to see what the disciples see but not being allowed to. Matthew uses 'righteous' where Luke uses 'kings'.

Peter writes that the prophets searched and investigated when they prophesied about the grace that was to come, and it was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you. This confirms Jesus' words that the prophets longed to see what is now revealed to the disciples.

The Letter to the Hebrews describes how the heroes of faith in the old covenant did not receive what was promised, but saw it from afar and greeted it – they longed for the fulfillment that the disciples now experienced.

The witnesses of faith in the old covenant did not receive the fulfillment of the promise, because God had something better in store for believers in the new covenant. This underscores Jesus' point that prophets and kings wanted to see what the disciples were allowed to see.

Isaiah prophesies that the people will hear and hear but not understand, and see and see but not perceive. Jesus contrasts this with the privilege of the disciples: they both see and hear what the prophets longed for.
Abraham's promise that all peoples on earth would be blessed through his offspring points forward to what the disciples now experienced in Jesus' coming – something Abraham himself longed to see.
Jesus says that Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and he saw it and was glad. This shows that the patriarchs and prophets longed to see the coming of the Messiah.
